legend: You are given an array of integers. You perform the following action exactly once: choose a non-empty subsegment of the array and order its elements in non-decreasing order.
How many different arrays can you obtain? A subsegment of an array is a collection of several consecutive elements.
input: The first line contains a single integer %%ZSMJ0%% — the size of the array (%%ZSMJ1%%).
The second line contains %%ZSMJ2%% integers %%ZSMJ3%%, %%ZSMJ4%%, ... %%ZSMJ5%% — the contents of the array (%%ZSMJ6%%).
output: Output a single integer — the number of different arrays you can obtain by sorting a subsegment once.
note: Listed below are all eight achievable arrays in the first example. Square brackets indicate the sorted subsegment.
